heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Burundi
heroData.subtitle: Hire compliant teams in Burundi without a local entity
heroData.description: Employer of Record (EOR) services in Burundi allow external companies to hire local talent legally. The EOR manages payroll, taxes, and social security (INSS) while you manage daily operations.
heroData.bestFor: Companies hiring 1-5 employees for market entry

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Drafting dual-language (Kirundi/French) local contracts complying with the 2020 Labor Code.

steps.title: OBR & INSS Registration
steps.description: Ensuring the employee is registered with the Office Burundais des Recettes and INSS for social security.

steps.title: Medical Examination
steps.description: Mandatory pre-employment check-up as required by local health and safety laws.

steps.title: Benefit Enrollment
steps.description: Setting up statutory health insurance (Mutuelle) and any supplemental private insurance.

steps.title: Work Permit Filing
steps.description: For expatriates, filing for the necessary 'M1' type work authorization with the Ministry.

items.title: Termination Laws
items.text: Strict 'just cause' requirements. Terminating without solid documentation of poor performance or gross misconduct leads to high severance payouts.

items.title: Probationary Limits
items.text: Limited to 6 months for management and 3 months for basic labor, non-renewable unless stated in the sector collective agreement.

items.title: Language Hierarchy
items.text: While French is standard for administration, Kirundi often takes precedence in local disputes; bilingual contracts are highly recommended.

faqs.question: Can I hire expats via EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but local labor preference laws apply. You must demonstrate that no Burundian national fits the role.

faqs.question: What is the standard work week?
faqs.answer: The standard week is 45 hours in Burundi, typically Monday through Friday and Saturday morning.

faqs.question: Are fixed-term contracts allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they convert to permanent contracts if they exceed 2 years or are renewed more than twice.

items.title: Minimum Wage
items.text: Varies by sector but generally updated slowly; check for the latest 'SMIG' decrees.

items.title: 13th Month
items.text: Not mandatory by law but customary in most professional and banking sector contracts.

items.title: Union Influence
items.text: Unions are active in the industrial and public sectors, often involved in collective bargaining.

steps.title: Input Consolidation
steps.description: Collecting overtime, bonuses, and unpaid leave data by the 20th of the month.

steps.title: IRE & INSS Calculation
steps.description: Applying occupational income tax (IRE) and social security deductions in BIF.

steps.title: Net Pay Approval
steps.description: Reviewing final net amounts to be paid to local bank accounts (e.g., KCB, BCB).

steps.title: Statutory Payments
steps.description: Wire transfers to OBR for taxes and INSS for pensions before the 15th of the following month.

steps.title: Pay Slip Issuance
steps.description: Distributing bilingual digital or paper pay slips to the workforce.

items.title: IRE Brackets
items.text: Income tax is progressive, with a 0% entry bracket up to BIF 150,000 and a 30% top bracket for high earners.

items.title: OBR Oversight
items.text: The OBR is highly digitized. Most filings are now required through their online portal to ensure transparency.

items.title: Currency Fluctuations
items.text: While contracts may be USD-based, actual payroll and tax clearing must be executed in BIF at the central bank rate.

faqs.question: What is the pay cycle?
faqs.answer: Burundi operates on a standard monthly payroll cycle, usually paid on the 25th-28th.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, all monetary benefits including performance bonuses and travel allowances are subject to IRE.

faqs.question: Is remote work supported?
faqs.answer: Yes, but if the employee is in Burundi, payroll must comply with local social security laws regardless of where the company is.

items.title: Housing Allowance
items.text: Many companies provide a tax-efficient housing allowance of up to 15% of basic salary.

items.title: Meal Vouchers
items.text: Non-cash meal benefits are common and generally carry lower tax burdens.

items.title: Bank Delays
items.text: Interbank transfers in Bujumbura can take 24-48 hours; plan funds arrival accordingly.

steps.title: Gross Input
steps.description: Defining the base BIF salary and any contractual bonuses or housing allowances.

steps.title: INSS Deduction
steps.description: Applying the mandatory employee social security rate (typically 4%) for pension and risks.

steps.title: IRE Brackets
steps.description: Calculating the Occupational Income Tax based on OBR's progressive percentage brackets.

steps.title: Benefit Offsets
steps.description: Accounting for Mutuelle (health insurance) contributions and any union dues.

steps.title: Net Generation
steps.description: Finalizing the net pay amount ready for bank-ready file generation (XML/CSV).

items.title: IRE Accuracy
items.text: Even small errors in income tax (IRE) calculation can lead to significant interest penalties from the OBR.

items.title: Fringe Benefits
items.text: The calculator must account for non-cash benefits (housing, transport) which are taxable in Burundi.

items.title: 13th Month
items.text: Calculators should be configured for 13th-month pay cycles, which are common though not strictly statutory.

faqs.question: Are tax tables updated automatically?
faqs.answer: Most cloud-based regional providers update BIF tax tables within 48 hours of an OBR budget announcement.

faqs.question: Does it handle multiple currencies?
faqs.answer: Yes, advanced tools allow input in USD/EUR with automatic conversion to BIF based on central bank rates.

faqs.question: Can I print pay slips from the calculator?
faqs.answer: Full versions provide OBR-compliant digital pay slips in PDF format.

items.title: Round-off Rules
items.text: The Burundian Franc (BIF) is usually rounded to the nearest integer in official OBR filings.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines
items.text: Calculator outputs should align with the monthly 15th-day reporting cycle for social security.

items.title: Expatriate Tax
items.text: Specific tax rules apply to foreign experts under M1 permits; ensure the calculator toggle is active.

steps.title: Official Gazette

items.title: Digital Portal
items.text: The API has significantly reduced the time to set up, but physical presence or a local POA is still necessary for signatures.

items.title: Banking Barriers
items.text: KYC procedures for foreign-owned entities can take weeks; local banks like Ecobank or Bancobu are common choices.

items.title: Free Zone Incentives
items.text: Companies exporting 80%+ of goods may qualify for the Free Zone regime with 0% tax for the first 10 years.

faqs.question: What is a SARL?
faqs.answer: Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) is the most common limited liability structure for small and medium businesses.

faqs.question: How long does API take?
faqs.answer: At the one-stop shop, basic administrative registration often completes within 2-5 business days.

faqs.question: Can I be the sole director?
faqs.answer: Yes, Burundian law allows for single-member SARLs (Société à Responsabilité Limitée Unipersonnelle).

items.title: NIF Requirement
items.text: The Numéro d'Identification Fiscale (NIF) is the most critical document for any commercial activity or contract.

items.title: Local Director custom
items.text: While not always legally required for SARLs, having a local resident director significantly eases banking and tax relations.

items.title: EAC Harmonization
items.text: Burundi's laws are increasingly aligning with East African Community trade and company standards.

items.title: Educational Hubs
items.text: University of Burundi remains the primary source for local academic talent, followed by several private institutes in 'Quartier Industriel'.

items.title: Cultural Fit
items.text: Emphasis on consensus-building and face-to-face communication in the local corporate culture is vital for successful hires.

faqs.question: Are private job boards common?
faqs.answer: Yes, digital boards are rising, but social networks like LinkedIn and WhatsApp groups are equally powerful for sourcing.

faqs.question: What is the notice period?
faqs.answer: Usually 1 to 3 months depending on seniority, as mandated by the National Labor Code.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay for advertising?
faqs.answer: Most agencies include standard job board postings in their success fee, but premium newspaper ads (e.g., Le Renouveau) may be extra.

items.title: Youth Workforce
items.text: Burundi has a very young population; graduate trainee programs are highly effective for long-term talent building.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.text: Awareness of religious and political holidays is key for scheduling interview cycles and start dates.

items.title: Mobile First
items.text: Recruitment communication is increasingly mobile-first; expect high engagement via SMS and mobile data apps.

faqs.question: Is cloud hosting safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the data center has high-tier security. Local Burundian firms increasingly trust AWS/Azure-based solutions.

items.title: Mobile ESS

items.title: Paperless Pay

items.title: Interoperability

items.title: Language Hierarchy
items.text: Accounting records must be maintained in French, which is the standard for both the OBR and local banks.

items.title: Currency Fluctuations
items.text: Tracking forex gains/losses is critical due to the volatility of the Burundian Franc (BIF) against the USD/EUR.

items.title: Digitization
items.text: The OBR is increasingly requiring digital submissions through their portal; manual bookkeeping is becoming obsolete.

faqs.question: What is the fiscal year start?
faqs.answer: The fiscal year in Burundi runs from January 1 to December 31.

faqs.question: Are international standards accepted?
faqs.answer: While the Plan Comptable National is used, many firms also prepare financial statements in accordance with IFRS for international reporting.

faqs.question: Do I need a local accountant?
faqs.answer: Yes, having a local partner registered with the OPC (Ordre des Professionnels Comptables) is highly recommended for OBR filings.

items.title: Plan Comptable
items.text: Burundi utilizes the OCAM based accounting system, though revisions are frequent to align with EAC standards.

items.title: Electronic Billing
items.text: The implementation of Electronic Billing Machines (EBM) is a current focus for the OBR to track sales data.

items.title: Archive Rules
items.text: Financial records and physical receipts should be archived locally for a minimum of 10 years per commercial law.

steps.title: API Renewal

steps.title: RCCM Updates

steps.title: INSS Audits

items.title: Tribunal de Commerce
items.text: The Commercial Court is the primary authority for entity governance filings; ensure physical stamps are obtained for all documents.

items.title: Local Substance
items.text: Regulators are increasingly looking for physical presence (office, local bank account) to confirm legitimate business activity.

items.title: Data Privacy
items.text: While still developing, awareness of data sovereignty is rising; ensure employee records are stored securely per regional EAC norms.

faqs.question: Is a local director required?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory for SARL structures, but highly practical for signing local tax and social security documents.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss a filing?
faqs.answer: Late filing fees at the RCCM are modest, but repeated failures can lead to the 'blocking' of your NIF, halting all business operations.

faqs.question: How often do I renew with API?
faqs.answer: The investment certificate typically has a multi-year validity, but performance reporting is often required annually.

items.title: Mandatory Insurance
items.text: Worker's compensation insurance is legally required and must be registered with the INSS and a licensed local insurer.

items.title: Bilingual Filings
items.text: While French is the primary administrative language, having Kirundi translations for site-level notices is a compliance best practice.

items.title: Physical Archive
items.text: Keep a bound 'Registre des Procès-verbaux' (Minutes Book) at the registered office for inspection by the Commercial Court.

steps.title: NIF Registration
steps.description: Securing your Numéro d’Identification Fiscale (NIF) immediately after incorporation.

steps.title: Monthly Declarations
steps.description: Filing income tax (IRE) and social security contributions by the 15th of each month.

steps.title: VAT Submission
steps.description: Submitting the 18% VAT declaration for the previous month's activities.

steps.title: Quarterly Advances
steps.description: Paying corporate tax installments based on previous year's performance or estimated turnover.

steps.title: Annual Finalization
steps.description: Conducting final tax audits and submitting the comprehensive annual return.

items.title: OBR Enforcement
items.text: The OBR is highly active; non-compliance or late filing leads to heavy automatic penalties and interest.

items.title: Free Zone Incentives
items.text: Companies registered in special economic zones may enjoy tax holidays and reduced rates for early years.

items.title: EAC Harmonization
items.text: Burundi is increasingly aligning its customs and excise duties with the East African Community (EAC) Common Market.

faqs.question: Can I file taxes online?
faqs.answer: Yes, the OBR portal allows for digital filing of most major taxes including IRE and VAT.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum tax?
faqs.answer: Yes, even companies in a loss position may be subject to a minimum tax based on turnover (e.g., 1%).

faqs.question: What is IRE?
faqs.answer: IRE stands for 'Impôt sur les Revenus d'Emploi', which is the occupational income tax deducted from employee salaries.

items.title: NIF Utility
items.text: A NIF is required not just for taxes, but also for opening bank accounts and obtaining a commercial lease.

items.title: Double Tax Treaties
items.text: Burundi has a limited but growing network of DTAs, primarily within the EAC and with select European partners.

items.title: Document Integrity
items.text: Ensure all invoices have the vendor's NIF and VAT status clearly marked to avoid deduction rejections by OBR.
